title: Proposed staged-release amendment
content:
# Proposed staged-release amendment

**Status:** Draft for resident review; not adopted or effective.
**Related case:** `WO-2a6bafff-7f89-47e2-b497-d5dc4519dd84`.

## Problem

The homepage case requires a published page and live verification. Its permit
requires an independent inspection before publication and a record of the
Pages result. The current permit policy requires every permit condition to be
met or not applicable before the formal inspection. The charter and council
delegation put the resident's merge after that inspection. Publishing from
`main:/docs` therefore cannot satisfy the case's live criteria before the
resident merges the page.

An independent preliminary inspection of the staged `docs/index.html`
passed and was filed as `ART-901392ee-384c-496b-84bc-eb118d9a6f6c`. It does
not replace the formal inspection or the resident's final acceptance.

## Proposed permit-policy text

The following is proposed for the "Completion, inspection, and acceptance"
section of `.city/policies/building-permits.md`. It is not a standalone
effective amendment: the prerequisites below must be resolved first.

> When a work order expressly requires evidence obtainable only after an
> authorized release, a staged release may be used if the resident expressly
> approves its scope, risk, release method, and outstanding obligations. The
> permit, class requirements, independent inspection, and applicable external
> requirements remain in force. A staged release is not final acceptance.
>
> Before release, an independent Building Inspector must inspect and record the
> exact proposed revision, its authorized scope, applicable pre-release permit
> conditions, and all criteria that can be assessed before release. A failure,
> unresolved material defect, changed revision, unauthorized action, or
> unavailable required authority stops release. Changed work requires a fresh
> independent inspection. The resident alone reviews and performs the
> authorized merge or release; agents do not merge on the resident's behalf.
>
> A preliminary notice must identify every permit condition exactly once as
> met, not applicable with reasons, or pending after release with a specific
> evidence and verification plan. Pending is not met or not applicable. The
> preliminary inspection must verify the notice and record outstanding risks,
> the verification owner, and an authorized response to failure. It does not
> waive unmet conditions or advance the case to final acceptance.
>
> After release, record the actual result and complete all post-release checks.
> The Engineering Manager then records a final completion notice addressing
> every permit condition as met with evidence or not applicable with reasons.
> An independent Building Inspector checks that notice, the delivered revision,
> all acceptance criteria, and the post-release evidence. Failures are returned
> for correction, not represented as passing. Only after a full final
> inspection may the resident record final acceptance. The resident may
> decline acceptance even if an earlier release was performed.

## Prerequisites and decisions

1. **Charter and delegation:** The charter's operating route says an inspector
   moves the order to `awaiting-merge` before the resident reviews and merges
   the pull request. The council-delegation policy states the same sequence.
   The proposed pre-final-inspection merge conflicts with that route. A policy
   amendment cannot override the charter. The resident would need to consider
   an explicit charter amendment and consistent delegation-policy amendments,
   with independent review and the normal genuine adoption process. No
   amendment or exception has been approved.
2. **Runtime support:** Installed Repository City 0.10.0 validates completion
   notice condition statuses as only `met` or `not-applicable`, and requires
   a current completion notice before entering `inspection`. It does not
   provide the proposed `pending after release` disposition or a separate
   staged-release lifecycle. A policy change alone cannot provide those
   capabilities. A compatible runtime change and its own authorization,
   delivery and inspection would be needed, or another independently reviewed
   procedure must be shown compatible without misrepresenting any condition.
   Do not hand-edit records or claim a pending condition is met.
3. **Existing case and permit:** An adopted amendment would not automatically
   establish its applicability to this already-authorized case or preserve the
   current authorization after changes to governance. Review the exact
   transition, permit, approval and versioning rules first; obtain any fresh
   resident decision required. Preserve earlier records and the original
   case `WO-ce0b2be1-7e0c-464b-b17c-814ad36e3ccd` unchanged.
4. **Hosting:** The existing decision permits only one static file and
   `main:/docs`, excluding other permission changes, paid services and
   outside-`docs` files. Host eligibility, address, actual costs and recovery
   remain unverified. Any additional scope requires a separate resident
   decision. Applicable legal and hosting requirements remain unresolved.

## Alternatives and risks

- **Split delivery and publication into separately authorized linked cases:**
  inspect and accept the file delivery first, then carry out publication and
  live verification under a separate case. This avoids changing the charter
  solely for this homepage but needs careful case preparation and may require
  fresh authorization; it must not silently revise or close either existing
  case.
- **No change:** keep the current case in progress and do not publish; no
  governance or runtime work is needed.
- **Staged-release amendment:** supports future cases whose evidence requires
  release, but changes general governance and potentially the plugin runtime.
  Early release can expose defects before final acceptance; the independent
  pre-release gate, resident-controlled release, explicit pending obligations,
  failure response and later independent inspection limit but do not eliminate
  that risk.

## Review requested

Review the proposed principle, charter conflict, runtime feasibility, impact on
the current authorization, and alternatives before any adoption or
implementation. A choice to prepare this draft is not approval of any charter,
policy, plugin, publication, or permission change. No vote, authenticated
identity, or adoption is implied.
